sēlectĭo , ōnis, f. seligo,
I.a choosing out, choice, selection (Ciceron.): “cum virtutis hoc proprium sit, earum rerum, quae secundum naturam sint, habere delectum: qui omnia sic exaequaverunt, ut in utramque partem ita paria redderent, uti nullā selectione uterentur, virtutem ipsam sustulerunt,” Cic. Fin. 3, 4, 12 ; cf.: “virtutem rerum selectione exspoliare,” id. ib. 2, 13, 43 ; “3, 6, 20: vitiorum,” id. Leg. 3, 10, 23 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
